faq.heroBody: It's a graphics-mod launcher for GTA 5 on Majestic and GTA5RP servers. Browse ready-made graphics packs (Redux), weapon model packs (Gunpacks) and pro-player setups, install any of them in one click and launch the game with the new look. Everything runs locally - we just drop the right files into your GTA folder, nothing else gets touched.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.q1: I just opened the launcher for the first time - what now?
gettingStarted.a1: Run through the short setup first - pick a language and a 3D background, then confirm where GTA 5 is installed. After that, sign in or just continue as guest - guests have full access to every build, no limits.
gettingStarted.a2: No, an account is optional. Without one you still install builds, mod the game, and add to favorites (stored locally). An account only matters if you want favorites synced across devices and to leave reviews.
gettingStarted.q3: The launcher couldn't find GTA 5 - how do I tell it?
gettingStarted.a3: On the first-time setup screen click 'Change folder' and point to your GTA 5 install (where GTA5.exe lives). Usually Steam → steamapps/common/Grand Theft Auto V or Rockstar Games → Grand Theft Auto V.

mods.title: Builds & mods
mods.q1: What's the difference between Redux and a gunpack?
mods.a1: Redux is a graphics mod: minimap, effects, color grading, time-cycles, FPS optimization. A gunpack is a set of weapon models (how guns look in the player's hands). They can be used together - they don't conflict.
mods.q2: Can I install just part of a Redux - only the minimap, say?
mods.a2: Yes. On any Redux page click 'Customize' - you choose what to install and what to leave from the author. The minimap has its own customization screen: HP/armor colors, size, position, custom PNG overlay.
mods.q3: Can I mix the minimap from one Redux with effects from another?
mods.a3: Yes. In minimap customization there's an 'Import from another build' button - pick any other published Redux and use just its minimap, leaving everything else from the current build.
mods.q4: How do I install gunpacks and pro setups?
mods.a4: Hit Install / Download Redux right on the build page. Progress is shown in the left sidebar. Once done, the build is applied automatically - your next GTA launch already runs the new graphics.

install.title: Install & remove
install.q1: Where does the launcher put files?
install.a1: Into your GTA 5 folder - alongside GTA5.exe the launcher creates the needed subfolders and copies mod files there. Originals get backed up so everything is reversible.
install.q2: If a mod broke / the game crashes - how do I roll back?
install.a2: There's an automatic recovery screen: if the launcher detects damaged or conflicting files, it offers a clean restore. You can also reinstall any other Redux on top - it'll restore its files and overwrite the broken ones.
install.q3: Do I need to close GTA before installing?
install.a3: Yes - close GTA 5 before installing/removing builds. A running game holds files open and install won't go through. After install you can launch the game right away.

safety.title: Safety & account
safety.q1: Will I get banned for using mods?
safety.a1: Graphics mods (everything in this launcher) are allowed on Majestic and GTA5RP - they're just texture/effect replacements with no cheat functionality. The anti-cheat sees these as regular graphics resources. Bans only happen for actual cheats and injectors - we don't distribute any of that.
safety.q2: Does the launcher collect my data?
safety.a2: Only what's needed to function: GTA path, picked build, your favorites. If you're signed in, your username and install history (just mod ids, never the files themselves) get stored on the server. The history powers the 'Recently installed' section in your profile. Want to wipe everything? The 'Reset cache' button in settings clears everything locally and signs you out.
safety.a3: On the sign-in screen click 'Forgot password?' - we'll email a code to the address you registered with. Enter the code and set a new password.

faq.ctaBody: Hop into our Discord or Telegram (icons in the lower-left of the sidebar) - both admins and other players answer fast. Found a bug? Hit 'Reset cache' in settings before reporting; that often fixes weird issues automatically.

rockstarMode.title: Rockstar Launcher mode
rockstarMode.description: For those who bought GTA V in Rockstar Games Launcher: it checks file integrity at launch and wipes mods. In this mode the game files stay clean, and mods are slotted in automatically the moment the game starts and pulled back out when you quit.

rockstarMode.staleWhatToDo: The button below takes the image apart without touching the game's new files, turns the mode off and refreshes the clean copy for the new version. After that install your build again and turn the mode back on - there is nothing left to restore the old version's mods from.
rockstarMode.methodCompare:
They differ in one thing only: who says "go". Everything else is the same - both keep the game files clean, store the mods on the game's drive and swap the file by an instant rename instead of copying gigabytes. The swap itself is equally fast and reliable in both.
Take "Automatic" if you don't want to remember anything: the launcher catches the game launch itself and cleans up after itself. Take "Manual" if you don't want a background task sitting in Windows Task Scheduler: then the two buttons before and after the game are on you.
rockstarMode.installBlocked: While the mode is on, installing mods is blocked. The game files are clean right now - a new install simply wouldn't stick. To install or change mods: turn the mode off here → install everything you need → turn the mode back on.

bypassTester.title: 🧪 Bypass test (temporary)
bypassTester.description: Checks which of the 5 DPI bypass strategies get through your network. We pull the first 256 KB of the installer with each method and measure time + speed. Handy if you sit in Russia and images/files do not load.
bypassTester.howToRead:
How to read this: OK = the strategy works. FAIL + Timeout = DPI is cutting it.
• Baseline OK → no bypass needed, you are not in a Russian DPI zone.
• TLS frag 3×/8× OK → current production covers you, fragmentation is enough.
• Only DoH OK → your provider does DNS poisoning, you need to resolve through DoH. Tell us which provider (Cloudflare / Quad9 / NextDNS) worked for you - we will add it as a fallback in the prod handler.
• ALL FAIL → the provider blocks at IP level; you need an external bypass (VPN etc.).

editor.removeAllTitle: Restore the minimap without editor tweaks

editor.ownHpColorHint: Unavailable: the gradient is on - it colors the HP bar itself
editor.hpGradientHint: Unavailable: turn off "Own HP color" and "Low HP threshold"
editor.gradNote: The bar color shifts smoothly with your HP percentage. Hit "Demo" to see it in motion.
editor.pulseLowHpNote: The HP bar blinks when health drops below the "Low HP threshold" value (25% if it's off).
editor.fontNote: GTA's own fonts: they work for everyone, nothing gets downloaded. The preview is drawn with them too - what you see is what you get in game. Shared by numbers and text.
editor.fontEmbedNote: This font isn't among the minimap imports - its glyphs get embedded right into minimap.gfx (+6…37 KB).
editor.fontNoCyrillic: This typeface has no Cyrillic letters - the text won't show in game. Cyrillic works with "Regular", "Like the GTA logo" and "Handwritten".
editor.textPlaceholder: Nickname or tag, Latin only, up to 32
editor.lowHpHint: Not available: the gradient is on - the HP color already shifts smoothly with the percentage
editor.hitOff: Turn the damage flash off completely
editor.hitPngNote: Your own PNG shows in its native colors - the game's red tint is removed automatically.
editor.hitDragNote: Or drag the white dot right on the stage.
editor.ringsExternal: The rings came with the redux. Flip the toggle off to remove them when you apply.
editor.ringsNote: Drawn around the player on top of the current minimap. They go on when you hit "Apply".
editor.blipsNote: The image replaces the sprite inside minimap.gfx itself (radar_centre / radar_waypoint): position and size stay native, the PNG fits in without distortion. The arrow spins with the player's heading - draw it nose up, ideally on a transparent background.
editor.gfxStock: Stock font right now. A font_lib_*.gfx file (FontLab and the like) will replace the font of the digits and text.
editor.screenNoSettings: settings.xml not read - pick the format with a button
editor.posHint: You can drag the HP bar and any HUD element. The position is in screen fractions, so it works at any resolution of your format. It counts from the edge of the safe zone, not from the edge of the screen - that margin is set on the right.
editor.sizesFromDb: Sizes come from verified layouts in our database.
editor.sizesFallback: Layouts from the database didn't load: the vanilla size is shown, but the size from the database goes into the game.
editor.safeProfilePending: Reading the setting from the GTA profile…
editor.safeChangeNote: Change the "Safe zone" slider inside GTA itself and the minimap will drift off, the layout will have to be applied again: the game file stores coordinates from the edge of the zone.
editor.transparentNote: Transparent: no backing, just the map with blips and the bars.
editor.outOfFrame: The map doesn't fit in the frame: in game the {{edges}} of the screen will cut it off. Move the box inward.
editor.sizesNotLoaded: The layout sizes from the database didn't load: the box is drawn vanilla ({{w}}×{{h}}), but the size from the database goes into the game - for formats other than 16:9 those are different numbers. Better to set the position after reopening the editor with a connection.
editor.safeNowWithPx: Now {{pct}} % of the screen on each side ({{x}} px horizontally and {{y}} px vertically on your screen). The game counts the HUD position from the edge of this zone: as long as it doesn't match yours, the preview and the game will drift apart. If the minimap in game ended up somewhere other than drawn here, move this slider and apply again.
editor.safeNow: Now {{pct}} % of the screen on each side. The game counts the HUD position from the edge of this zone: as long as it doesn't match yours, the preview and the game will drift apart. If the minimap in game ended up somewhere other than drawn here, move this slider and apply again.
editor.safeProfileOk: In the GTA profile the "Safe zone" slider sits at {{n}}. We don't convert that number into a margin yet: two testers measured 1.5 % and 5 % at the same step, so which way the game counts - we're still checking.
editor.safeProfileFail: Couldn't read the setting from the GTA profile (the game hasn't been launched yet or the profile wasn't found) - the margin sits at {{pct}} %, that's either your manual setting or the fallback 5 % (the max of GTA's scale).
editor.sceneHint: Drag the elements with the mouse - they snap to the edges and the center of the map (a line lights up); hold Alt to move freely, without snapping. Center (buttons in the toolbar or the C key) puts the selected element exactly in the center of the map. Fine tuning: arrows - by 1 unit, Shift+arrows - by 10. The checkerboard is the transparent area (in game the world is there). You can't go above the top edge: the game cuts off everything out of frame.
editor.saveHint: One slot, stored on your computer. Nothing is published - it is a way to bring the look back if you experiment and lose it.

editor.ownArmorTrough: Own color for the empty armor part

serverBanner.title: Can't reach our server
serverBanner.body: The launcher couldn't reach the main (European) host or the backup one. Usually the route to our domain gets cut by your provider, DPI or an active VPN - the server itself is alive. Check your internet, turn the VPN off, then open Settings → Servers and network: it shows which host answers, and the region is switched there too (in Russia - RU).
